title: Managed Disks and Application Storage
description: Learn about Azure managed disks for VMs and how to choose the right disk type for different workloads.

data.text: Azure Managed Disks are block-level storage volumes managed by Azure and used with Azure Virtual Machines. Unlike unmanaged disks that tied VM and storage account together, managed disks are standalone resources. You choose a disk type based on your performance and cost requirements.

Every VM has an **OS disk** that stores the operating system and boot files. You can attach **data disks** for application data, databases, or logs. Data disks can be added or removed while the VM is running, giving you flexible storage expansion.

data.title: Create a Managed Data Disk with Azure CLI
data.content: Create and attach a Premium SSD data disk to a VM
data.code:
az disk create \
  --resource-group rg-demo \
  --name myDataDisk \
  --size-gb 128 \
  --sku Premium_LRS \
  --os-type Linux

az vm disk attach \
  --resource-group rg-demo \
  --vm-name myVM \
  --name myDataDisk

data.title: Initialize a Data Disk on Linux with PowerShell
data.content: Format and mount a new data disk from inside the VM
data.code:
Invoke-AzVMRunCommand \
  -ResourceGroupName "rg-demo" \
  -Name "myVM" \
  -CommandId 'RunShellScript' \
  -ScriptString @'
    sudo fdisk -l
    sudo mkfs -t ext4 /dev/sdc
    sudo mkdir /mnt/data
    sudo mount /dev/sdc /mnt/data
  '@

terms.definition: A high-durability block storage volume managed by Azure for use with VMs.
The disk that stores the VM operating system and is required for every VM.
An optional disk attached to a VM for application data, databases, or logs.
A host-level cache (None, ReadOnly, ReadWrite) that improves I/O performance for certain workloads.

data.title: Sizing Matters
data.text: Once you create a disk, you can increase its size but not decrease it. Start with a size that covers your projected growth to avoid downtime from resize operations.

data.title: Exercise: Attach a Data Disk
data.description: Provision a VM, attach a data disk, and format it from the guest OS.
steps: Deploy a Linux VM in the Azure Portal.
Create a 64 GB Premium SSD data disk and attach it.
SSH into the VM and list disks with `lsblk`.
Format the new disk, create a mount point, and mount it.
Verify you can write files to the new mount.
data.expectedOutcome: A running VM with an additional mounted data disk ready for application data.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Managed disks are standalone Azure resources for VM storage.
Choose disk types based on IOPS, throughput, and cost requirements.
OS disks boot the VM; data disks store application data.
You can attach and detach data disks without stopping the VM.
data.takeaway: Managed disks give you predictable, scalable block storage for every Azure VM workload.
